relevance_note: The paper describes named patients with HA20 ("Stool samples were obtained from 16 patients with HA20 and 15 of their family members") and gives individual-level data (sex, age, severity, stomatitis, abdominal symptoms, medication) for 16 patients and 15 relatives in Supplementary Table 1, but prints no TNFAIP3 variant for anyone.
method_note: Supplementary Table 1 was transcribed cell by cell; every span was then verified to occur verbatim in the paper file (grep). No TNFAIP3 variant is printed anywhere in the paper for any patient, so each of the 16 patients gets a variants row with variant_original_string 'not reported' (D-22); no variant rows are made for the 15 relatives, whose variant status is not stated. Labels: the paper's own IDs P3-P22 (Supplementary Table 1, 'The current ID of the patients is the same as the ID at the previous report (1).') and relative IDs '<patient>-fa/-mo/-sib' ('P, patient; fa, Father; mo, mother; sib, sibling'). One relative, P8/P9-mo, is the mother of two patients; the paper gives one label only. Scope: relatives are in scope as relatives of patients ('15 healthy family members', 'healthy relatives'). The 18 patients mentioned as participating include P1, P2, P6, P14, P15, P16 (inferred from the list 'patients 3-5, 7-13, and 17-22' plus the 16 patients of Supplementary Table 1); these six are described nowhere individually (only their clinical characteristics 'were previously reported'), their variant status is unknown, so they get no rows and are only counted in cohort_size_as_stated (36 individuals) and n_patients_reported (22 patients with HA20 in the prior report). The paper never says that P1, P2 or P6 were tested. Contradiction: the abstract and the Results say 16 patients and 15 family members, but one Results sentence says 'Thirty-one fecal samples from 16 patients and 15 healthy family members were sequenced' while Supplementary Table 1 lists 16 patients and 15 relatives (31 rows). The checklist item 'oral ulcers' is recorded from the table column 'Stomatitis' (yes/no), the only oral finding; the paper never uses the word 'ulcer'. 'abdominal symptoms' is recorded as a phenotypic feature only, not as 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation', because the paper states 'not all patients with HA20 received gastrointestinal endoscopy, and so alternative indicators such as the disease severity or abdominal symptoms do not necessarily reflect the exact intestinal condition'. The column 'Antibiotics use from 6 months to 4 weeks ago' records antibiotic exposure, not infections, so no 'recurrent infections' item is inferred from it. Ages in the table are ages at stool-sample collection ('sex, age at the sample collection'), recorded as age_at_last_evaluation; no age at onset or at diagnosis is given for anyone. The separator ' / ' does not occur in any table of this paper, so D-31 raised no issue; the two stacked header blocks of Supplementary Table 2 (phylum counts) are used only for the order of the patients. The Discussion sentence about 'one refractory patient [who] successfully received hematopoietic cell transplantation (Shiraki et al., 2021)' concerns a previously published person with no individual-level fact, so no row was created. Disease label and clinical_diagnosis_basis are 'not reported' for the relatives, described only as 'healthy family members'. The relative P22-sib is the 'excluded younger brother (P22-sib)' with food allergies.
